subject: AWS offer: CTA wording, metering notes, and launch artifacts
messages:
From: Lara Chen <lara.chen@acme.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AWS listing: final CTA + billing footnote?

Michael / Kim —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the AWS offer draft. I reviewed the hero and bullets this morning and we have two immediate asks from our procurement and engineering teams before we can sign off: 1) a concise CTA variant that drives trial vs contact-sales paths (we'd like to A/B test these on the listing), and 2) explicit metering/billing language for per-token vs per-minute inference so our finance folks can map to internal chargebacks.

Can you send a short set of CTA options (one-liners, and a 2-line supporting subtitle) and a one-paragraph billing footnote? If you have a copy table or matrix, that'd be ideal. Also, any thoughts on calling out Copilot/assistant integration as a capability in the bullets — our product folks think it helps conversion but AWS listing space is tight.

Lara
Director of Product, Acme Financial
Attachment: none

---

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Apr 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS listing: final CTA + billing footnote?

Hi Lara —

Thanks — attached are the working artifacts: product_page_draft_v2.docx and pricing_table_v3.csv. I also included a quick CTA matrix (see cta_matrix.xlsx) with variations targeted at trial-driven vs sales-driven flows. Summary below:

- CTA variants (short):
  1) "Start a free trial" — direct, best for product-led conversion.
  2) "Request a live demo" — better for larger enterprise prospects.
  3) "Try inference in your account" — AWS-native phrasing, helps set expectation.

- Supporting subtitles (two-line):
  - Trial variant: "Deploy one-click inference with guaranteed throughput. No credit card required for the 14-day trial."
  - Demo variant: "See a walk-through with your dataset and SLA needs — schedule in 2 clicks."

- Billing footnote (draft one-paragraph):
  "Billing: Charges are calculated per inference unit. Short requests are billed per token; long-lived streaming or session-based usage may be billed per-minute for dedicated deployments. For customers using Dedicated capacity, usage is metered against reserved units — contact your account team for custom pricing and metering mappings."

- Copilot mention: I recommend a single-line capability callout in bullets (not in hero): "Integrates with assistant/Copilot workflows for low-latency, context-aware responses." Keeps hero clean but surfaces it to technical buyers.

Lara — please see the Drive link for commentary and let us know which CTA you prefer for the initial A/B. Internal team: Kim / Marissa / Jonas — can you review the footnote for legal/ops clarity and confirm we can map tokens -> chargeable units with our AWS billing guidance?

Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1abcDEFanalytics
Attachments: product_page_draft_v2.docx (docx), pricing_table_v3.csv (csv), cta_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

Best,
Michael Grant
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

---

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Lara Chen <lara.chen@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Apr 2028 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS listing: final CTA + billing footnote?

Michael / team —

Thanks for the draft. Quick notes from listing ops & legal POV:

1) CTA wording: prefer option 3 "Try inference in your account" as primary CTA on AWS. Rationale: aligns with AWS UX and reduces confusion around "free trial" semantics in Marketplace offers. Keep "Request a live demo" as a secondary action in the listing (link to scheduling page).

2) Billing footnote: tighten the language to remove ambiguous terms. Suggested revision (single sentence + parenthetical example):
  "Billing: Charges are applied per inference unit — short requests billed per-token, and session/streaming usage billed per-minute on Dedicated instances (e.g., a 60s stream on a 2-core session will count as X minutes). Contact your account team for custom reserved-capacity arrangements and to map usage to internal chargeback codes."

3) Metering SKU: we need one SKU for API tokenized usage and one SKU for Dedicated subscription blocks (AWS private offer). Suggest names: REDWOOD-TOKEN-MONTHLY and REDWOOD-DEDICATED-UNIT. Please confirm with finance before finalizing the SKU labels — those go into the offer metadata.

4) Copilot/assistant mention: include a short bullet but avoid the term "Copilot" in the hero — AWS policy sometimes prefers neutral phrasing. Suggested copy: "Supports assistant and tool-driven integrations for contextual agents."

5) Accessibility & listing constraints: reduce hero sentence count to max 140 characters. We should do a second pass to compress benefit bullets.

Attaching a quick CTA matrix showing which option maps to which SKU and backend routing.

Attachment: cta_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

Kimberly Park
Marketplace Programs, Redwood Inference

Kim / Michael / Lara —

LGTM — two small tweaks from GTM copy side:

1) Hero subtitle for the Trial variant: replace "No credit card required for the 14-day trial." with "Start a 14-day trial with no credit card." (shorter, clearer for mobile).
2) For the copilot bullet, use: "Works with assistant workflows and plugins" — avoids trademarked names while still signaling capability.

If Lara confirms the CTA preference (Try inference in your account) we'll push the final assets to the marketplace packet and send to AWS onboarding.

Marissa Cole

Hello Michael and Lara,

Thanks for the update. To complete the AWS Marketplace offer submission we need the finalized offer metadata, the SKU mapping, and the public-facing hero/call-to-action copy. Please confirm the primary CTA and upload the following artifacts to the shared onboarding bucket:

- Final product page copy (PDF or DOCX)
- SKU list and pricing table (CSV)
- Support & SLA summary (one-page PDF)

Once uploaded, please open the DocuSign envelope linked below to accept the standard offer terms. After we receive the documents and the signed envelope, the usual review window is 3–5 business days.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/ACME-AWS-Offer
Onboarding bucket: s3://aws-marketplace-onboarding/acme-redwood/

If you prefer, we can do a 20-minute checklist call on Monday to walk through the final fields.

Regards,
AWS Marketplace Seller Support
Attachment: none
